messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Incident INC-2026-07-21-11: p99 latency for /v1/stream on shared-gpu-pool-7 = 8.9s (SLO 5s). p95 = 3.6s. Streaming stalls and reconnects reported. Auto-pager to #incidents + oncall.

leila: Acked, I'm oncall. Noted streaming errors and 502 bursts. Tom/Andrea please run quick health checks for shared-gpu-pool-7. Any recent infra changes?

tom: Checking deploys. No model rollouts. Infra deployed blkio policy tweak ~40m ago to default lower weight for fairness (500->250). Also kernel NVMe scheduler update landed in canary earlier today and promoted 2h ago to prod nodes 6-8.

andrea: I'm seeing node-7 with high iowait and queue depth. KV cache misses spiking, followed by many rebuffer events on streaming. Likely IO related.

leila: Can we surface per-container IO and top open sockets on node-7? Need to identify noisy tenant quickly.

andrea: Pasting quick snapshot:
```bash
# short snapshot from node-7
CONTAINER   TENANT     CPU%   MEM%   NVME_R/s   NVME_W/s   OPEN_SOCKETS
c-314       tenant-314 69.8   21.0   3200       90         4800
c-201       tenant-201 4.1    4.2    34         2          140
c-5         tenant-5   1.8    1.0    6          1          60
```

andrea: blkio stats for c-314:
```text
Read: 520MB/s
Write: 12MB/s
io_wait: 20%
throttled: yes
```

andrea: tenant-314 is doing massive batched context fetches + long-running generation. Appears to be the noisy neighbor.

leila: Alright. Immediate mitigations: 1) throttle tenant-314 IO and cap concurrency, 2) enable model-fallback to gpt-lite for streaming on pool while we stabilize, 3) prepare migration to dedicated-escape-3 if needed. Andrea, can infra-bot apply cgroup changes?

infra-bot: @leila Applying cgroup throttle for container c-314: setting blkio.weight=80 (from 250) and blkio.throttle.read_iops_device=4000. Reducing concurrency for tenant-314: 18 -> 6.

leila: Push fallback rule: route streaming sessions > 2s latency to gpt-lite-stream. Tom, can you roll that?

tom: Pushing route-fallback now with threshold p95>2.0s for /v1/stream on shared-gpu-pool-7. Rolling in 30s.

andrea: Metrics 2m after throttle/fallback:
```text
p99 -> 4.8s
p95 -> 2.1s
node-7 nvme read -> 160MB/s (was 520)
io_wait -> 6%
streaming stalls -> down 70%
```

andrea: Improvement but tail still above SLO. Some backend storage read latencies remain elevated; looks like object-store GET latencies spiked concurrently. Could be correlated but tenant-314 was main driver.

leila: CS: any customer reports?

cs-liaison: Two customers reported streaming glitches; one enterprise opened a ticket and wants ETA. We've notified them that we're mitigating and may migrate offending tenant. Billing flagged possible SLA claim.

leila: Ok. Recommend live migration of tenant-314 to dedicated-escape-3 now to fully remove noisy neighbor. This will cause ~20-45s session churn. CS approves?

cs-liaison: Approved. Notifying affected customers before migration.

infra-bot: Starting migration: `migrate-tenant --tenant tenant-314 --from shared-gpu-pool-7 --to dedicated-escape-3 --drain 25s --preserve-cache=false`

andrea: Migration progress: checkpointing 10% -> rsync KV 46% -> reroute traffic 79% -> complete.

infra-bot: Migration finished. Old container drained. Tenant-314 now on dedicated-escape-3.

tom: Post-migration snapshot (5m):
```text
p99 -> 3.0s
p95 -> 1.5s
node-7 nvme read -> 48MB/s
io_wait -> normal
streaming stalls -> down 94%
```

leila: Great. Keep throttles and fallback in place for a 20m stabilization window, then relax increments if metrics hold. Andrea/Tom: follow-ups — (1) investigate kernel NVMe scheduler change impact; revert on node-7 if we can reproduce, (2) tighten per-tenant IO burst limits and add early alert for blkio throttle events, (3) add routing rule to prefer dedicated pools for tenants with sustained high IO.

andrea: I'll open INFRA ticket to rollback or test scheduler in canary and run fio reproduction with tenant's pattern. Also adding per-tenant IO histograms to alerting.

tom: I'll add a CI gate for blkio/default-change with synthetic multi-tenant test. Also capture tenant-314 workload signature for future auto-detection.

cs-liaison: Customer comms sent: interim note + ETA for full postmortem. Enterprise customer requested latency histograms and timeline for SLA review; forwarding to ops and billing.

leila: Handing off incident ownership: Andrea/Tom own postmortem; CS-liaison and Sam handle customer follow-ups and billing. I'll remain incident lead until SLOs stable for 30m. If regressions occur ping @leila.

sam: Noted. Will prepare final customer-facing timeline and share postmortem draft.

infra-bot: Incident state -> mitigated. Monitoring for 30m.

leila: Closing active page for now. Thanks all. Follow-ups tracked in INFRA-4022 (scheduler), INFRA-4023 (per-tenant IO), and PLATFORM-771 (routing heuristics). :white_check_mark:
